decision.explanation: The reference views that best distinguish the supplied conditions are the Welch/persistence spectral shapes, carrier-band envelopes, wavelet/STFT timing, and kurtosis localization. Q01 is outside all three reference patterns: it shows a regular broadband impulse train at about 3.54 Hz with harmonics across several carrier bands, a dense spectral group near 0.94 kHz, Pearson kurtosis 8.008, and filter-bank excess kurtosis up to 18.768 in the low/mid-frequency bands [Q01.C01.S0001, T01.envelope_1, T01.envelope_2, T01.envelope_3, T01.envelope_4, T01.stft_detail, T01.wavelet, T01.kurtosis_bank]. Nearest-reference controls conflict: R04 is nearest in baseline Welch and persistence, while R03 is nearest in wavelet, cepstrum, envelope_1/2/4/5 and several other signatures; these are forced rankings without an acceptance threshold and do not establish known similarity. The decisive evidence is therefore the measured modulation frequencies and kurtosis values, supported by the time-frequency images, rather than any single distance. Cyclic summaries are relatively close by raw-distance control, but Q01's maximum coherence is much higher and deterministic periodic impulses can themselves produce cyclic coherence [T01.cyclic, R02.cyclic, R03.cyclic, R04.cyclic]. Orders and synchronous averages are unavailable for Q01 and every reference because no independent RPM trace was supplied, so no rotational-order, phase-locking, bearing-frequency, component, or severity claim is supported [T01.orders, T01.synchronous, R02.orders, R02.synchronous, R03.orders, R03.synchronous, R04.orders, R04.synchronous].
